name: COODU AI
line: India-first AI company. The front door existed before the first model did.
problem: No public presence. No narrative. One founder, and every decision routed through him.
approach: Next.js and GSAP, one scroll-driven narrative. Alongside it, a structured knowledge base — vision, roadmap, pillar docs — so the founder's context stopped living in the founder.

name: HELM
line: A business operating system. Six modules that refuse to be six spreadsheets.
problem: Small businesses run on a dozen disconnected sheets and WhatsApp threads. Nothing reconciles. Nothing is auditable.
approach: One FastAPI backend. Six domain modules behind a shared auth and data layer. Docker, so deployment is one command.

name: HERALD
line: Email in, WhatsApp out. It reads the forty emails. You get the one.
problem: The important email always arrives while you're nowhere near an inbox — and buried under forty that aren't.
approach: A Python service ingests the mail, classifies it, summarises it, and pushes only what survives that to WhatsApp as a thread you can act on.

name: SITE ATTENDANCE
line: Face-recognition attendance on construction sites. The conditions do not cooperate.
problem: Paper muster rolls on remote sites: unverifiable, slow to reconcile, and trivially gamed.
approach: On-site face onboarding and a 1:N matching pipeline, with a supervisor review step. Built for bad light and worse networks.

name: COODU TRUST
line: A donation platform. The money has to arrive.
problem: Non-profit donation flows break in the least forgiving place possible: at the payment step, on a stranger's phone.
approach: Rebuilt the front end and hardened the donation path end to end. Environment-driven endpoints, no hardcoded hosts, deployable on shared hosting.

name: TOPROCK PORTAL
line: Spreadsheet sprawl behind one dashboard. The sheet still runs underneath, and nobody has to look at it.
problem: Creative pipeline status lived in a Google Sheet nobody trusted and everybody edited.
approach: A read-through dashboard on the Sheets API, with OAuth. The sheet stays authoritative. The team gets an interface instead of a grid.
